page: The Amazon Web Services r8in.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), and cryptographic primitives. Memory configuration consists of 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes a 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero GPUs, and no bundled local instance storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional memory and parallel execution capabilities. Cached small-block memory read bandwidth reached 7,701.13 GB/s, while uncached large-block reads yielded 385.73 GB/s and writes reached 155.8 GB/s, placing the server within the top tier. Multi-core performance is marked by a stress-ng multi-core score of 103,377.69 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 628.33 GB/s. In-memory data structures perform effectively, evidenced by Redis SET throughput of 172.22 million operations per second and static web throughput of 215.23 GB/s. For CPU-based machine learning, AMX and AVX acceleration yield top-tier prompt processing throughput across small (4,432.34 tokens/s), medium (316.46 tokens/s), and large models (41.2 tokens/s), though token generation speeds fall into average to strong percentiles.

The absence of internal NVMe storage necessitates external EBS volumes for persistent data, shifting the primary architectural tradeoffs to remote storage latency and configuration. However, the 150 Gbps network pipe ensures high throughput to remote volumes and distributed clusters. Resource efficiency is driven by the dense RAM allocation and high-throughput Intel silicon, making the r8in.24xlarge suitable for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, distributed caching tiers, and memory-bound CPU inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 48-core, 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocking at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro system. The server incorporates 768 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and a 150 Gbps network interface, while operating without discrete GPUs or local ephemeral storage. Hardware extensions include AVX-512 and AMX matrix accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for uncached memory read bandwidth (385.73 GB/s), Redis execution (172.22 million SET operations/s), and multi-core parallel decompression (628.33 GB/s). While single-core throughput is balanced, parallel CPU performance and memory throughput are strong. This makes the r8in.24xlarge well suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, memory-intensive big data analytics, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
